newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee dips vs dlr in spot, forward at noon.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee dips vs dlr in spot, forward at noon.

text.p: The Indian rupee was down against the dollar in both the spot and forward markets in noon trade on Monday, dealers said.
They said dollar demand pushed the rupee down to 35.79 per dollar in spot deals in morning trade before it recovered.
In latest deals, the rupee was quoted at 35.78/79 against opening quotes of 35.76/77.

"There has been some buying from a large corporate and also a leading financial institution," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "But dollar supplies remain good and any dip in the rupee is proving to be temporary."
In the forward market, deliveries for months beyond December were in demand, dealers said.

"I think the far forward months had fallen to unrealistic levels," said a dealer. "It was mainly speculation ... there was no genuine receiving interest. It is now headed back to more correct levels."
In latest deals, January-delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 0.72 rupees and February at 0.82 against opening quotes of 0.70 and 0.80 respectively, dealers said.
